entries.claim: Task 4 says the AC3 case "also pins that a missing reading doesn't reset", but neither that case nor Task 3's missing-percent case can tell "a missing reading leaves the next point alone" apart from "a missing reading resets it to the first point". So D-06 and the must-be-true "A turn with no fill reading shows nothing and moves nothing" (line 28) have no check that can fail.
entries.failure_scenario: Suppose the hook is written `const p = e.context.percent ?? 0` or `if (!(p >= first)) next = first`, so a missing reading resets the next point to 33. Task 3 feeds 33 (toast, next=43), then missing (buggy reset to 33), then 43: the toast still fires, so the test passes. Task 4 feeds 33 and 43 (next=53), then 10 (reset to 33), then missing (buggy reset to 33, no change), then 33: the toast still fires, so the test passes. The bug ships. In a session, a turn with no reading after a toast at 33 then lets a reading of 34 to 42 toast again, which breaks REM-03's 10-point hold-off. Only a sequence like 33, missing, 40 expecting no toast at 40 would catch it, and no task has one.

entries.claim: Task 2's Verify expects `claude plugin validate` to list the three `userConfig` fields, but validate in 2.1.330 never lists userConfig fields, so this part of the Verify cannot be met as written and checks nothing.
entries.failure_scenario: I ran `claude plugin validate` (text and `--json`) on an installed mod whose plugin.json declares 11 userConfig fields, including two `number` fields (agile-mods). The manifest section printed only `Validating plugin manifest: <path>`. Its JSON `manifest` object holds only errors, warnings, notes, gatingHooks, wasm and modules, with no field listing. An executor running Task 2 never sees the promised listing, so it either reports a false failure or skips the check. Either way nothing confirms the three fields and their bounds were read.
